You found an old rural property that seems abandoned. The front door is open and there are signs the residents left in a hurry. On a table lie a photograph of a family and a partially burnt note.
"If anyone finds this, please, do not enter the barn..."

Among the belongings left in the Morrison house there is a diary written by Helen. The first pages tell of the days before the collapse: Robert was worried about the news and Daniel wanted to leave the property to look for help in town. Go upstairs and look for the diary.
"Robert locked the barn. He doesn't want Emily near it. He says it's to protect her."

The barn is shut from the inside. There are bloodstains on the wood and tools scattered on the floor. Something happened here. Perhaps Robert was trying to keep something away from the family. Enter the barn, but beware of what is still inside.

A trail of tire tracks leads to an abandoned vehicle on the road. The plate matches the car mentioned in Helen's diary. In the glove box there is a fuel receipt and a photograph of Daniel. The young man apparently tried to leave the property alone. Go to the vehicle and investigate.

A note in Daniel's vehicle mentions a neighbor named Walter, one of the last people to talk to Robert before the family isolated itself. His house looks looted. There are bodies scattered across the property and a message written on the wall.

Walter left a note saying Helen sought medical care a few days after the outbreak began, with injuries and a fever. The clinic records may reveal what happened to her. Go to the clinic and look for the records.

Among the medical documents there is a note about Emily: Helen wrote that her daughter was scared and that Robert had prepared a hideout for her. Investigating the shelter you find drawings, toys and a small hidden backpack.
"Daddy said he will come back to get me. I am waiting."

Emily's hideout holds a note from Robert: he would go out to look for fuel and medicine and come back before nightfall. The last clue points to a cabin used by hunters. The place is surrounded by the dead. Perhaps Robert made it here, but never managed to return.

After gathering every clue, you return to the farm. Behind a fallen piece of furniture there is an envelope that went unnoticed. The letter was written by Helen. But the noise of the search drew the dead to the house: survive them and read the letter. You finally understand what happened: the family tried to survive in isolation, but fear, illness and lack of supplies destroyed everything.

"Robert did not return. Neither did Daniel. I hear noises in the barn every night. I have no strength left to go on. Emily is with me. If anyone finds this letter, know that we tried until the end."

Investigating the barn again, you find the remains of an improvised barricade and one last note from Robert:

"I should have taken everyone away while there was still time. I tried to protect my family, but I ended up trapping us all here. If anyone finds these words, do not make the same mistake. Do not wait until it is too late."

The farm is silent once more. You gather what can still be used and leave the place behind.
